fields.meta_title: Donation Request Form Builder for Businesses | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a donation request form that checks lead time and your giving budget, routes each ask to the right manager, and follows up after the event.
fields.h1: Build a Donation Request Form That Sorts Every Ask
fields.hero_description: Build a donation request form that takes asks from schools and charities and checks each one against your giving policy.
fields.features_heading: What a Business Checks Before It Gives
fields.features_subheading: Every group asks in its own way. Emergent builds the form and the giving log that sort each request before a manager reads it.
fields.feature_1:
Policy questions come before the ask

Ask for the event date, the group's EIN, and its exemption letter before the request itself. The app checks the date against your lead time and files the letter with the request.
fields.feature_2:
Each ask checked against the year's budget

Set one giving budget for the year. Every request shows the amount already committed and what would be left after a yes. The approver sees that balance before deciding.
fields.feature_3:
Requests routed by store and by amount

Send each request to the manager of the store the group picks. Anything above that store's limit goes to a regional manager by email, with the full request and its letter attached.
fields.feature_4:
Cash, gift cards or products, asked apart

Let each group choose cash, a gift card, products, or a sponsorship. Each type asks its own questions, such as logo placement for a team sponsor or retail value for a raffle prize.
fields.feature_5:
A decision email the group can act on

Approve or decline from one email. The app writes back to the group with the decision, plus pickup details for a gift card or the date the check goes in the mail to them.
fields.feature_6:
The codebase, exported on paid plans

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository on paid plans when giving requests need to sit next to your other systems. Host it where you like and keep building on top of it.
fields.why_description: A template collects the ask. Emergent builds the rules a business gives by, and keeps every request in a database you own.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Businesses, Four Kinds of Ask
fields.tab_content_1:
Gift card asks need 30 days or more, and this one gave 51

School auctions ask Oxbow Tavern for gift cards. The Sedgewick Elementary PTA wants a $50 card for its Mar 14 auction, 51 days out. The tavern turns down any ask under 30 days. This one clears that line, with the PTA's EIN and exemption letter attached. Owner Dario Pellandini gets an email that a request is in.
fields.tab_content_2:
After $750 for jerseys, $900 is left

Brackett Brewing sets aside $6,000 a year for team sponsorships, and $4,350 is already committed. Eastside Under-12 Soccer asks for $750 toward jerseys with the brewery's logo on the sleeve. Marketing lead Wren Hatchett opens it from a Slack alert and sees $900 would be left for the year after a yes.
fields.tab_content_3:
By store and by amount, a $400 ask reaches Marcus

Hollis Hardware runs 6 stores, and each store manager can approve up to $250. The Fairhaven Little League picks Store 4 on the form and asks for $400 in field supplies. Anything over the $250 limit goes to regional manager Marcus Trell. He gets the email, and the Store 4 manager is copied.
fields.tab_content_4:
Which three groups have not sent a photo?

Kestrel Bakery approved 9 donations this quarter and wants to know what each one did. The app emails every group 14 days after its event to ask what the event raised and for one photo. Six groups have answered. Owner Beatriz Coulter-Ames sees the 3 still waiting on one list and sends each a second email from it.

faq_plan.q: What is a donation request form?
How do I create a donation request form?

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable PDF forms from single businesses and foundations, a WPForms template a business puts on its site so nonprofits can ask it for a donation, and how-to-ask articles (Springly, an in-kind letter guide). Every result is the blank sheet; none shows what a business does with forty requests a season. This page is for the business or company that receives donation and sponsorship requests from schools, teams and charities: a form that asks for the event date, the ask and the group's EIN and exemption letter, holds a lead-time rule, checks each ask against the year's giving budget, routes each store's requests to its manager, and follows up after the event. Donors giving money stay on the donation form page and gift receipts on the donation receipt page.
tab_stories: Fennimore Tavern gives gift cards to school auctions; the Ashgrove Elementary PTA asks for a $50 card for a Mar 14 auction 51 days out, which clears the tavern's 30-day lead time, so the app emails owner Dario Pellandini an Approve and Decline request.

Wickham Brewing sets $6,000 a year for team sponsorships and has committed $4,350; Eastside Under-12 Soccer asks for $750 toward jerseys, the app shows $900 would be left after it, and Wren Hatchett approves it in Slack.

Hollis Hardware runs 6 stores; each request goes to the manager of the store the group picks, and the Fairhaven Little League ask of $400 at Store 4 is over the $250 store limit, so it goes to regional manager Marcus Trell.

Kestrel Bakery approved 9 donations this quarter; 14 days after each event the app emails the group to ask what the event raised and for one photo, and 6 groups have answered while 3 are still waiting.
